transcript.answer:
ADR-002 (accepted 2026-09-25) settled this when it rejected PR #261 review comment 4098626654, which asked to drop the card and let the model phrase the answer. Otto renders delivery status deterministically as a card for three reasons.

1. Measurement. The card-rate KPI (SC-006, at least 90% by 2026-Q4) counts cards. A prose answer has no denominator, so the KPI can't be measured. The thumbs-up KPI (SC-007, at least 80%) also depends on the card, because ratings attach to card turns and a prose answer produces none.
2. Compliance and trust. The EU AI Act data-flow record and the docs/danish-review.md rows promise that the customer reads delivery status verbatim from the TMS. A model-paraphrased delivery time or ETA is a hallucination this pilot cannot afford.
3. Spec change. FR-043 of support-agent-tms-tools is being amended to allow a deterministic-render tool. The assistant stays suppressed for this answer.

The not-found card is deterministic too, because the model cannot invent a shipment it did not fetch. The reviewer's concern was that a rigid card reduces the model's flexibility. The ADR judged that cost acceptable.
sources: issue-318 (Add tools for handling "Hvornår bliver min booking XXXXX leveret?")

judgements.reason: The answer covers both essential points, the card-rate KPI (SC-006, ≥90% by 2026-Q4) needing card turns as the denominator and the compliance promise that TMS status is shown verbatim so a paraphrased ETA is an unaffordable hallucination, and it notes that free text was proposed on a PR, with nothing that contradicts the gold.
